The bug has been fixed and verified in accordance with the requirements in [summary.txt](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/csv_3_group_b_fix/summary.txt).

### Root Cause
In [`Lexer.java`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/csv_3_group_b_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/csv/Lexer.java#L87-L115), the `readEscape()` method returned the read character directly in its `default` branch instead of verifying whether the character is a configured meta-character (delimiter, escape, quote, or comment marker). Consequently, unexpected characters (such as `'N'` in `\N` or `'a'` in `\a`, as well as non-quote characters preceded by an escape character) were treated as valid escape sequences, causing the escape character to be swallowed.

### Fix
Updated `readEscape()` in [`Lexer.java`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/csv_3_group_b_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/csv/Lexer.java#L108-L116) to check if the escaped character is a configured meta-character using `isDelimiter(c) || isEscape(c) || isQuoteChar(c) || isCommentStart(c)`. If it is not a meta-character, `readEscape()` returns `END_OF_STREAM`, signalling [`CSVLexer`](file:///Users/nothing/prometheus_workdir_microstudy/csv_3_group_b_fix/src/main/java/org/apache/commons/csv/CSVLexer.java) to output both the escape character and the subsequent character verbatim.
